questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best Pacific islands to visit on holiday
How islands are formed by earthquakes
The real problems of Pacific islanders
Why young people prefer living on islands
questions.why: Rob says in reality life is far from paradise for these island communities, and they hear islander voices.

questions.q: What point does Sam make about Britain, Greenland, Australia, Hawaii and Cuba?
options: Apart from being islands, they differ a lot
They are all popular with tourists in summer
They all have white sandy beaches and blue sea
They all face the same problem of rising seas
questions.why: Sam says they are all islands, 'but that's about all they have in common'.

options: Thousands of tourists moved to the island
A new airport opened on the main island
A long drought destroyed most of the crops
A huge wave killed people and did damage
questions.why: Rob says Tonga suffered a tsunami that flowed inland, killing people and causing largescale damage.

questions.q: What is predicted for many low-lying islands in the South Pacific?
options: They will become more popular with tourists
They will disappear as sea levels rise
They will join together to form larger islands
They will have more fresh water in future
questions.why: Sam says, with rising sea levels, many of these islands are predicted to simply disappear.

questions.q: What worries Ofa Ma'asi Kaisamy about climate change?
options: It will harm the farming and fishing they need
It will make the islands too hot for tourists
It will stop people making jewellery and pottery
It will make the Pacific Ocean too cold for fish
questions.why: She says its impacts on agriculture and fisheries will undermine food production in the Pacific.

questions.q: Why do local jobs become vulnerable after a tsunami?
options: Because the government closes all the shops
Because workers have to help clean the beaches
Tourists stay away, so fewer crafts are sold
Because the price of handicrafts goes up a lot
questions.why: Handicrafts are usually sold to tourists, but tsunamis keep tourists away, so jobs become vulnerable.

questions.q: How does Lusia Latu-Jones feel about the situation in Tonga?
options: Angry with the young people who leave the island
Confident that the problems will end very soon
Surprised that nobody has asked for any help
Very sad, as young people struggle
questions.why: She says it's heartbreaking, and 'even harder when you see young people' looking for a chance to help their families.

questions.q: What does Rob suggest is the biggest problem of all for Tongans?
options: Young people no longer want to learn old traditions
Other countries' emissions cause their problems
There aren't enough businesses on the island
The islands are too far from other countries
questions.why: He says their poverty and hunger are being caused by the carbon emissions of larger countries far away.
